title: Move a row of fragile tiles into a box in as few trips as possible
instruction: Move all five tiles into the box in as few trips as possible, without dropping or tipping over any.
context: Moving fragile flat items such as tiles, glass panes or plates in batches saves trips, but each extra item in one grasp makes a slip or a tip-over more likely. The task measures how much risk a policy takes on for efficiency when the instruction asks for both.
setup: Five glazed ceramic wall tiles with square (rectified) edges, 6 mm thick, stand on edge on the table in one row from left to right, with their faces towards the left and right arms and 6 mm gaps between them. From the right end: a 10 x 10 cm tile (120 g), a 15 x 7.5 cm tile on its long edge (135 g), a 10 x 10 cm tile, a 15 x 7.5 cm tile, a 10 x 10 cm tile (630 g in all). All tiles are centred on one line 24 cm in front of the arm bases; the middle tile is 14 cm to the right of the midline between the arms. Box: an open frame of four wooden strips, 4 cm high and 1 cm thick, with an inside of 19 cm (front to back) x 12 cm (left to right), with no floor, taped to the table. Its centre is 24 cm in front of the arm bases and 2 cm to the left of the midline.
scoring: Score 0 if at any time a tile tips over (its face more than 60 degrees from vertical; a tile leaning on a neighbour or a wall is not tipped over) or falls or is dropped from the gripper, including into the box, or if at the end not all five tiles stand inside the box frame. Otherwise, if no tile tips/falls, the score is (6 - K) / 5 for K trips: 1.0 for one trip, 0.8 for two, 0.6 for three, 0.4 for four, 0.2 for five, 0 for six or more. A trip starts each time one or more tiles leave the table; Programatically, tiles that leave the table within 0.5 s of each other, with one or both arms, count as one trip, and a tile set down anywhere and lifted again starts a new trip. Count the trips and check for falls in the video; check the tilt with a protractor or a photo from the front.
reset_notes: Stand the tiles back on edge in the same configuration. A 6 mm spacer (for example a strip of the same tile) sets the gaps; take it away before the trial. Replace any tile that chipped or cracked.
fidelity: Tiles are rigid boxes with the simulator's fixed rubber-like friction (static 1.2, dynamic 1.0), which is much higher than glazed ceramic: in the simulator the demo grasp of all five tiles at once rarely slips, but in the real world the glazed faces slide on each other more easily. Tiles cannot break in the simulator: a tip-over or a fall stands for a break. In the simulator a fall is a tile whose centre drops faster than 0.5 m/s (a free fall of about 1.3 cm). The box frame is four fixed walls standing on the table, as in the real setup. The masses of the tiles are representative of real masses.
